correctness.rationale: Reduce modulo p²: the conditional sample consists of p⁴−p² equally likely primitive pairs. When y is zero modulo p, x is a unit and every form is a unit. Otherwise, writing z=x/y, a form can be divisible by p only at its two simple unit roots if its slope is a nonzero square modulo p. Each represented square slope thus occupies two separate projective directions of mass 1/(p+1) each. In either direction a matching form allows exactly one of the p residual lifts of z, by the nonzero derivative 2z modulo p. Two such lifts coincide exactly when the slopes agree modulo p², since the congruence is z²=t_i. A coherent fiber keeps 1/p of the mass in its two directions; an incoherent one keeps none. This gives the stated conditional density including s=0, where there are no exclusions. Every incoherent fiber needs a second form, so h≥max(0,2s−k); the bound is realizable for all allowable s≥1 with two distinct unit lifts on the required fibers and repetitions for any excess forms. The objective s−max(0,2s−k)/p is strictly increasing, with slopes 1 and 1−2/p>0, giving s=m and the exact equality criterion, including saturation k≥p−1. Independently enumerated the forbidden residue pairs and all 12031 unordered families of unit slopes modulo p² across (p,k)=(3,1…5),(5,1…4),(7,1…2), including nonsquare slopes and repeated forms. The exact minima, all minimizers and joint counts agreed.
residual_risks: The supplied verifier's random families use only square slopes; the independent check includes nonsquares and the analytic argument covers all permitted unit coefficients. No p=2 or global claim was checked or inferred.

value.rationale: A simultaneous local test on a common primitive input cannot in general use a product of single-form factors, or even reconstruct the answer from the slopes modulo p alone. The exact formula identifies the second residue digit that matters and gives a sharp nonzero floor, the exact family size needed to reach it, and all extremizers. This is useful for bounding local obstructions uniformly with many constraints; the parameter range and the extremal gap are natural, not just selected finite instances. No downstream global conclusion is needed or asserted.
residual_risks: Restricted to odd good primes and primitive pairs; the formulas do not imply any global squareful asymptotic or Euler product convergence.
